- ## Biboom *—* 2024/4/27 11:56

  -Crosshair placement is consistently inconsistent. I might need to look at comp or other DM vods, but for this particular game it's all over the place. Either you're not focused or it's just bad.    -I suggest going a lot slower when clearing angles. Like, a LOT slower. You're constantly rounding corners (W + A/D when peeking) with your crosshair not correctly prefired or sometimes just completely off the mark.  -No real strafe patterns that I could see other than when trying to "play off a corner". When you're out in the open, you fully spray and crouch.   -This isn't entirely bad because you do have decent mouse control but it's very noticeably costing you duels when added to the previous issues in your readiness/preparation. It makes you rely too heavily on flicks, and bullet rng in some cases. -Speaking of flicks, you're way too pressed. There's little to no target confirmation when firing.   -Again, this isn't the end of the world if you were to just fire a few taps and then adjust while moving and THEN burst/spray. However, since you have the habit of instantly committing to a spray, by the time you've adjusted to the enemy's head your recoil has already gotten out of hand and it's just a "Jesus take the wheel" kind of deal at that point.    -Check out any Hooj's video on target confirmation where he talks about "the circle". Basically you can go fast in small flicks close to your crosshair but need to slow down and microadjust more attentively with medium-long range flicks.

  just a couple things I noticed in your deathmatches:

  - I wouldn't peek with ADS, I would rather HOLD an angle with ADS. ADS gives you better accuracy at the cost of movement speed, so you're actually strafing slower if you're peeking ADS.
  - I need you to strafe more in between bursts. You should immediately strafe after firing bullets, no matter if you killed the enemy or not. Otherwise, you're standing still for too long and you're going to get killed.
  - Your microflicks could be faster but that can be improved with aim trainers.

If you can, try to look at how pro players DM and pay attention and try to copy or replicate how they prepare for fights, while taking the fight, and what to do after. Look at how they move in the fight (do they A D strafe spam or not, counterstrafe or not, hold W when peeking or not), how their crosshair placement looks on different angles (how high it is and how it changes depending on elevation). For me, I looked at how f0rsaken moves when he sees an enemy and how he wins the fight (he moves unpredictably because as soon as he sees an enemy, he strafes in the opposite direction of the enemy's swing direction and sometimes crouches to throw their crosshair placement off). 

- ## Mang Tomas *—* 2024/3/25 06:24

  For DM:

  > Aim:

  - Your crosshair kinda floats around on angles where enemies can't possibly swing out of from (In the middle of two angles)
  - Crosshair placement is pretty low sometimes
  - Microadjustments are sometimes there but mostly just resort to shooting bodies
  - Slow mouse control. I get that people say calm aim is better than flicky aim but your aim is not calm and more like lazy and slow (no offense) Look at Yay and Demon1's mouse control, they have pretty low sens (.27 800 dpi for yay and 0.1 1600 dpi for demon1) but they are fast and smooth
  - Practice rounding or tracking the outside of corners and only pre-aim if the corner you are about to swing is a long straight angle

  

  > Movement:

  - Peeking while holding W
  - Not knowing when to crouch spray or commit to spraying
  - Counterstrafing will help your shooting error go down and actually make your shots hit. (A lot of blue on your shooting error graph)
  - Practice aiming while moving (Aiming should be done before stopping your movement so all you have to do is shoot)

  

  > Mental

  - Peeking an angle and not being ready to shoot
  - In a DM, or in any of your games, always anticipate that an enemy could be holding the angle you are about to swing

- ## Mang Tomas *—* 2024/3/24 07:32

  Hello, here's what I noticed -There's a difference to taking your time to aim and taking too long to aim. -Crosshair placement still pretty low sometimes specially on elevated terrains. Playing more DMs should fix this since I saw in your tracker you only have 7.4 hrs of playtime in DMs. -You need to brush up on angle advantage and stop peeking too close to the wall. If you are going to peek close to the wall, peek wide and don't stop until you aim your crosshair on the head while on the move. -Movement looks pretty decent, but when first burst don't hit, you tend to stand still way too long.  Also, idk if this is intentional and how you usually peek this angle, but please don't shift peek close angles where you think enemies will be.(If you are actually not holding shift, then this peek looks way too slow) (3:53) -When holding angles, please don't just stand still close to the wall. Peeker's advantage exist in this game and you are not hitting a guy swinging at full speed (4:04). If you are actually holding an angle, try to always be mobile and strafe in intervals (not spamming ADADAD but A, wait, D, wait, A, wait, D) it keeps you focused an enemy swinging and makes it harder for them to kill you since you are moving

- ## Holmster [AIM], *—* 2024/3/5 14:07

  @NEBULArctic Hello! I hope you find my input insightful. For starters, is there any particular reason you are playing without sound? I’ve found that playing dm without sound doesn’t help train your brain to correctly comprehend and respond to audio stimuli. I would consider turning sound back on for your DM’s. Your mechanics are pretty decent. However there are a few things I noticed while watching the vod.

  1. You tend to shoot well before you are ready. Meaning, either your crosshair is not on their head yet, or you have not stopped moving yet. This is causing your first bullet accuracy to suffer. Examples: the neon at 1:36 and 1:44. Notice that the second fight was won completely by random chance.

  

  1. Your crosshair placement is a bit low generally. Try to bring it up a bit higher, and you’ll see more headshots.

  

  1. You aren’t always ready. When playing dm, you want to be in a permanent state of expecting the re-fragger. Always expect another enemy to be coming around the next corner.

  

  1. You look uncomfortable. In any action, whether that is peeking, moving during gunfights, or even tapping bullets, you look a bit off. To fix this, try following Woohoojins movement guide, and just play the game more!

  Overall, I would recommend playing more dm while working on some of these things I’ve mentioned. I’m sure you will be a big jump in general comfortability when taking gunfights! Good luck!

- ## Dannew *—* 2024/2/27 02:02

  The main thing we can work on is that we rush out shots. Some of these fights lack proper target acquisition. For example: All of the frames are counted from the frame where (You or Derke, which is used as an example later) starts aiming. Frame 0:http://puu.sh/K1J2u/7fce5a829a.jpg Frame 5: http://puu.sh/K1J2z/a5580f8e4e.jpg Frame 6: http://puu.sh/K1J2A/87d624b914.jpg There is no way we saw that we were on him and tried to micro readjust. We just flicked and clicked. We should be, flicking to the head, then micro readjusting if needed and if not needed then click. One frame is 16.6ms in a 60fps recording. No human can react that fast. Here is another one: (flick starts): http://puu.sh/K1J39/0fae83c351.jpg (flick is done): http://puu.sh/K1J3b/5517d4f42c.jpg (The next frame after the previous one): http://puu.sh/K1J3e/fe39b4e533.jpg We need to take our time to make sure we are on the targets head. We don't need 100% accuracy but if we get onto the target with a flick and we fire the frame after we simply got lucky if we get the kill and unlucky if we didn't. Flicks can be practiced to become more consistent but they are never going to become consistent enough to depend on. Flicking is used to get close to the target as fast as we can to give us time to micro readjust. Here is an example of a very similar peek but executed by Fnatic Derke Frame 0: http://puu.sh/K1J5M/5eac4dab1c.jpg Frame 5: (this is when your flick is already executed in some of your fights): http://puu.sh/K1J71/60d169559f.jpg Frame 12: http://puu.sh/K1J5V/b924549a72.jpg Frame 13 (this is the frame he fires in): http://puu.sh/K1J62/875863a580.jpg You can watch it in full speed for yourself if you want: https://youtu.be/US_A3Z4MaxE?si=dKheGInxrXFMkpbp&t=479 Summary: Practice taking your time to fire, make sure you are close enough to the target when you decide to stop. Close enough means that after we have started slowing down all we have to do is micro adjust and then fire. (not flick and fire)

- ## Dannew *—* 2024/2/7 21:46

  You tend to stop and then aim after you already slowed down enough to able to fire an accurate bullet. Here is a heatmap of your the enemies heads position (Green) at the point we slowed down enough to be fully accurate. Only dotting the first initial stop at each encounter https://puu.sh/K0rFR/bb23d495c9.jpg 2 examples to show what I mean by this  https://puu.sh/K0rGq/053741a906.jpg  https://puu.sh/K0rGf/b5c9d6509d.jpg We don't need to stop and then aim We should try to aim while slowing down or pre aim right or left of the head and make sure that the movement while slowing down will move the crosshair onto our enemies head. This enables us to stay mobile for longer and still fire an accurate bullet before we are standing still on their screen. It only takes 80ms to get from full movement speed with a vandal to being slow enough to be accurate. That is very fast. Way faster then it takes us to aim which means we can spend more of the time moving aiming and then stop at the time where we have gotten close enough to their head and all we need to do is micro-adjust which we can do while slowing down and fire when it is all been done. I did not include all peeks and all the fights you had, fights I didn't count were for example: Fights where you died without being able to slow down enough to be accurate and a few more. The sample size isn't big so don't take it to an extreme. This is not a method that shows if you do this well or bad but simply a way for me to visualize it a bit easier. You could of done this great but had an even worse heatmap of this specific thing but I found this specific issue before I choose to show it in this manner. For reference here is a heatmap of a recent game of mine at which I think I did do this quite ok. (It's on a different map and DM is DM so take it all with a grain of salt) https://puu.sh/K0rFW/690b9595c6.jpg I also fail to make sure that it is close to the enemies head when I stop but I try to do so rather then aiming after stopping. If it means I have to walk a few extra ms then that will just make me a harder target to hit while saving me roughly the same amount of ms on the time it takes me to aim. Regardless of how fast and consistent I think I can get my aim to it won't beat simply moving a few ms extra to make sure I'm close to their head when I'm about to micro adjust or simply fire. Here is a merged version of both the heatmaps: https://puu.sh/K0rGa/e4d14ffc87.jpg and here is the DM at which I took my heatmap from: https://youtu.be/UK43hBlwlFs (You don't need to watch it, it's just there so I can't be coping and make shit up) If we remove the most extreme from both (I removed 2 from you because he wasn't even looking at you anyway) We end up with these areas which show the range we would have to re-adjust within: https://puu.sh/K0rKn/2565fc3b15.jpg The more faded boxes show the easiest 50% of all the adjustment that have to be made due to the crosshairs position at the time we have already stopped. It becomes clear that 50% of the time I get a drastically easier re-adjustment to make. Conclusion: *From what **I** can tell* you need to try to adjust your crosshair while moving to end up closer to the enemies head before initiating to stop or during in worst case scenarios. This will make it so you get to micro-adjust shorter distances while slowing down rather then having to either flick which you do end up doing in some fights or spend time standing still aiming which you also end up doing a few times. We rather want to try flicking initially to the angle or the fight in  which we try to land closer to the enemies head to get as close as possible so we can micro adjust while slowing down instead. PS. It's nothing personal, I'm not comparing you to me or the opposite. I only used myself because I had a DM Vod I could use to create the heatmap and it let me double check that I was doing this myself ![🙃](https://discord.com/assets/460d0ae35d91aed8.svg) . Pretty sure you are higher ranked either way.

- ## Salzi *—* 2024/2/3 15:02

  As someone who is a very good aimer in Valorant aswell as specifically in aimtrainers, I can tell you that smooth/clean aim is much better for consistency, also you often slowwalked instead of just peeking an angle, which might get you more kills and maybe make you win, but a dm is not supossed to be won. In a deathmatch you want to put yourself into an uncomfortable situation and still through mechanics (aim and movement) win the fight because this is where you will be often in games by just being forced into them. You also often crouch sprayed which generally is good in close range, but only then, in longer fights you dont want to crouch nor spray what you want to do is to burst in 2-3 bullets and move to the side. For the slowwalking in dms I'd recommend playing without sound or very little if you need to hear your own gun. I can also give you decent aimtraining playlists (if you dont already use ones from Voltaic or aimerz) that will make you imrpove your smooth aim a lot more.

- ## OsOsOsOs *—* 2024/1/30 14:47

  Hi, You need to start being very conscious of whether your crosshair is at head height or not. Most of the shots throughout the VOD are centre mass. Stop counter strafing, it does not help you in this game and you will have much less movement error if you stopped this. I am not saying dont strafe, i am saying dont use D key to stop movement towards left and vice versa. You get too surprised when you see an enemy. When you are in fight mode, you need to be ready that if an enemy pops up on your screen, you will be able to fight them calmly. This comes down to expecting where an enemy might be. This is specially easy to do in DMs because the spawn points are set and easy to read most of the time. One big movement issue i saw was the you take small steps when you try to peek into an angle. This is a bad habbit that will cost you rounds as your enemies get better. Take bigger steps and peek confidently, its fine if you over peek an angle and get exposed a little too much because this will fix itself in time as you build muscle memory of how an angle is to be peeked.  FOCUS ON POINTS IN THIS ORDER

  - Crosshair needs to be on head height.
  - Stop counter strafing
  - Take big steps when peeking angles
  - Expect enemy locations

  Looking forward to watching a full game VOD. All the best in your games. @Schroedinger's Aza

It looks like you're trying to "slice the pie", but you're not quite doing it correctly. Your slices tend to be way too big, and in return you force yourself to make bigger flicks, or you peek into multiple angles at once. Note that when you peek into multiple angles at once it also takes longer for you to recognize where an enemy is on your screen and adjust to it. Force yourself to slow your peeks down! Every "slice" you make should be smaller, and you should be pre-aiming your crosshair and convincing yourself that there is an enemy where you are about to peek. I can record myself doing this in an exaggerated way like how you need to practice.

- ## keithsnowblob *—* 2024/1/6 12:48

  Just looking at your pre-round coordination, it's pretty obvious that you comm very little on both offense and defense. You seem to be taking fights a lot by yourself, and this may be why you feel as if your confidence starts diminishing sometimes. I think the main things you should focus on to improve are your communication and utility usage. Firstly, on communication, you don't have to make very extensive plans to win rounds. You can just come up with simple sentences like "Hey Kayo, can you flash for me A main and we peek together?" or "Hey Reyna, can you flash out and then I'll blast pack out." Start simple. SImple easy plans that help you coordinate with 1 or 2 players will really help you in your games. I see that you're aggressing mid doors a lot on defense which is pretty textbook. There are two ways to make that fight easier for you. Either use your utillity such as nade or boombot to isolate a fight, or even better just double up with a teammate and swing together. This ensures that you're not peeking into a 1 V 2, which will help you win the mid-doors fight more easily. You asked about your peeking habit as well, but I feel like the problem isn't with how you're peeking, but more the way you take the fight. For example, you have a habit of insta-crouch spraying when you're panicked, which might cause you to lose the fight more easily. You could try and calm yourself down, and then peek to ensure this doesn't happen. Overall, I think your aim is pretty good, but if you just slow down a bit and calm down a bit I'm sure you'll be able to rank up quickly. One last thing I noticed is your economy management. You seem to force up when you lose the pistol round which caused you to lose on defense 0-3. Usually when you lose pistol you save so you can buy on the third round to ensure that you win 1-2. However, if you do want to force, force with the entire team to maximize your chances of winning that round.

- ## Bike *—* 2023/12/15 19:14

  Round 17: You just can't be lurking with the op. You need to peek so many dry angles that it's just unoptimal. You should be going with your team or holding a flank angle. Preferably going with your team. It's a miracle that chamber missed you shift peeking through the harbour wall. The kill on jett is fine though in contrast. You do get properly punished for peeking so many angles by the sage. Peeking angles is the op's greatest weakness, and you should seek to minimize this weakness by peeking as few angles as possible. Round 18: I like this round a lot more, however in post you should be holding drop earlier, as that is playing to the strengths of the op. You have very little impact on this round by waiting until someone dies to drop to hold it. Round 19: In post, I'd like to see you holding an angle with the op instead of being in your camera. Being in your camera is strong when you can peek off of it, but with the op peeking off of the camera is actually disadvantageous. Round 20: This round is only okay if you had a genuine read that they would peek you b main, otherwise I'd rather you go with the team or pick up a vandal and lurk Round 21: Unlucky timing, however if you are going to be double lurking with chamber, I think using a vandal would be better. If we're truly minmaxing, I think you should cage off that angle before walking up, but this is probably too hindsighty to do in a real game. After you kill the chamber, you need to commit to an angle and hold it. Round 22: This round is fine. You die to a movement error by staying crouched, but other than that this round is okay. Round 23: Not your fault that you're caught out by the sage, gecko should have cleared top wall. This round is good.

  **ATTACK** Round 13: If you want to throw that cam, you need to go with the team. just peeking out of b main at 1:17 is way too slow, the round is basically over before your flank even starts. if you had gone with your team you could have traded out the chamber. Round 14: They can jump both of the trips you placed in preround. Your lurk is once again too passive, you hear a guy running away at 1:22 but since you're way too slow on your lurk you can't capitalize whatsoever on this. It's clear after you open the door that you don't think you can win as you just walk through a smoke, through a cypher trip, into 4 holding c alone. This round was still winnable, and you threw it all away. Round 15: You need to be commiting against the sage here, fighting so passively gives her a chance to avoid the duel. On an eco you want to be able to get as many fair duels as you can, and this duel against sage is likely to be the best fight you can take the whole round Round 16: You start your flank so far away that you can't cancel it. You need to commit to the flank here and trust that they're caught off guard. You aren't going to be able to help on the site exec so rejoining your team is pointless and too slow. After you rejoin your team you just sit in cam where your teammates are peeking deeper angles. This is too passive and leads to you having low impact on the round. It's a similar story with how you're holding flank. If you're that worried about flank and you don't trust your trip I'd go to play on site with your teammates. Best case scenario with you holding flank is you get a dry 50, worst and most likely case you have no impact on the outcome of the round. Even when you spot both you hold a super passive angle where you wouldn't be able to trade your teammates.
